newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi defends former PM Andreotti on trial.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi defends former PM Andreotti on trial.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has come to the defence of Giulio Andreotti, the country's seven-times premier now on trial for alleged links to the Mafia.

Prodi said in an interview published on Sunday with the German newspaper Welt am Sonntag that he could not believe Andreotti, a leading Christian Democrat, allegedly protected the mob during his long career, as charges against him claim.
Asked if he "could imagine that a man who was seven times prime minister could have supported the mafia and ordered murders," Prodi answered: "No, it is extremely difficult for me to imagine this,"
"I have faith in justice, but I am losing sleep over this whole affair," said Prodi, who briefly held a post as industry minister during Andreotti's fourth government in 1979.
Prodi's comments were criticized on Sunday by one of the prosecutors in Andreotti's trial.

"Every time there is any type of external, extraneous influence to the trial's procedures, there is a risk of alteration," anti-mafia prosecutor Roberto Scarpinato said in an interview with La Repubblica newspaper, which asked him about Prodi's comments.
"It seems difficult to venture an evaluation without knowing. One can offer an opinion, but one has to take into account that one speaks without knowing."
During the trial, which began in 1994, arrested alleged Mafia killers have come to the stand and testified that Andreotti was the mob's political protector between the mid 1960s and mid 1980s.
Andreotti denies the charges, saying they are part of an elaborate Mafia plot to punish him for crackdowns on organised crime by governments he headed.
